findings.body: The doc comment promises `Shorten text to at most limit characters`, but the truncation path can return `limit + 1` characters: `head` is built from `text.chars().take(limit)` (up to `limit` chars) and then an ellipsis character is appended. When there is no space in `head`, `format!("{head}…")` yields exactly `limit + 1` chars; when there is a space the prefix is shorter, so it usually fits, but the no-space branch does not. The test at `a_long_string_stops_on_a_word_boundary` even asserts `out.len() <= 21` for `limit = 20`, so the +1 is baked in. Because the stated purpose is fitting under a hard GitHub ceiling, a caller passing that ceiling as `limit` can produce a title one character over. Either reserve one character for the ellipsis (`take(limit.saturating_sub(1))`) or fix the doc to say `limit + 1`.
findings.rule: Return Result<T> using the crate error type
findings.title: shorten can return limit+1 characters, breaking its own contract

value.summary: The multibyte-slicing fix in `shorten` is sound and `first_sentence` is safe, but `shorten` violates its own `at most limit characters` contract on the no-space branch by appending an ellipsis to a `limit`-character head, yielding `limit + 1` characters — a problem when `limit` is a real ceiling such as GitHub's check-run title cap. The test even encodes the +1. No other issues found in this file.
